title: Resolve review discussions
summary: Review discussions can point to a specific line or behaviour. Resolving one should mean the concern has been addressed or an agreed decision has been recorded.
introduction: Review discussions can point to a specific line or behaviour. Resolving one should mean the concern has been addressed or an agreed decision has been recorded. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Review discussions can point to a specific line or behaviour. Resolving one should mean the concern has been addressed or an agreed decision has been recorded.

blocks.code:
Reviewer: what should appear for a query containing only spaces?
Author: treat it as an empty query
Change: trim the query before filtering
Check: add the spaces-only case
blocks.title: Resolve review discussions

blocks.text: The discussion leads to a clear behaviour and a check. The review history explains why trimming was added.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a reply when you need more detail to understand a review concern.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not mark a discussion resolved only to make an unresolved question disappear.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
